title: Hygroscopy
description: Some salts pull so much water from the air that they dissolve into a puddle of their own brine. Packets of silica gel and the salt on winter roads work this way.
effect: some substances pull water out of the air
pickWhy: Borderline: a useful effect, but known since antiquity with no clear discoverer or date. Renamed from Deliquescence to the broader effect.
edbDesc: Deliquescent materials are substances (mostly salts) that have a strong affinity for moisture and will absorb relatively large amounts of water from the atmosphere if exposed to it, forming a liquid solution.
